findings.why_it_matters: Both normative constants in 15.27.3 (E function returned value rules 1 and 3) carry an embedded ZERO WIDTH SPACE (U+200B) inside the digit string, at the point where the PDF line was re-flowed. The character is invisible when rendered, so a human reading the markdown sees the correct value, but any mechanical use of the transcription -- grep for the constant, copy/paste into a test golden, or a script that parses the literal -- gets a string that is not a number and will not match. These are the only two U+200B characters in the entire 8000+ page transcription, so this is a localized artifact and not a transcription convention. Digit counts were verified against the rendered page: rule 1 = 31 digits after the point, rule 3 = 33 digits after the point; both match the PDF exactly once the U+200B is removed.
findings.suggested_repair: Delete the two U+200B characters (byte offsets ~2030029 and ~2030380 in specs/ISO_COBOL.md) so the lines read exactly '(2 + 0.7182818284590452353602874713526).' and '(2.718281828459045235360287471352662).'
